message.reasoning:
I need to write JUnit 4 tests for FormElement covering its key methods: elements() and addElement() as simple accessors, submit() with its branches for action URL resolution, validation of a non-empty action, and HTTP method handling for POST vs GET, plus formData() which needs to handle empty and multi-element lists along with tag-specific filtering logic.

Within formData() there's more to account for—skipping non-submittable or disabled elements, handling select elements with single/multiple selections or none selected, checkbox/radio handling based on the checked attribute, and defaulting values for normal inputs. Since FormElement is part of the real jsoup codebase, I'll test it using actual HTML parsing through Jsoup.parse() to construct realistic form elements rather than mocking anything.

I'm setting up a test using an HTML form with named inputs, verifying that formData() extracts the correct name-value pairs, and I'll also parse with a base URI to test submit() and absolute URL resolution.

Rather than relying on remembered bug-fix tests, I want to build my own coverage: constructing a FormElement directly to check addElement() and elements(), confirming formData() returns empty for a form with no elements, and verifying that non-submittable tags like a div added via addElement are properly skipped by formData() based on Tag.isFormSubmittable().

I also want to test skipping disabled inputs, skipping inputs with missing or empty names, and thoroughly cover select elements -- checking that multiple selected options all get added with set=true, that the first option is chosen when none are marked selected, and that a select with zero options behaves correctly.

I need to verify checkbox and radio behavior across checked, unchecked, and checked-but-valueless states (where the latter should default to "on"), plus normal text input handling via val(). Then I'm moving into form submission tests, checking that action attributes resolve to absolute URLs with GET as the default method, and that explicit method="post" attributes get picked up correctly.

I also need a test confirming Validate.notEmpty throws when both action and baseUri are empty, and another confirming the baseUri is used as a fallback action when no action attribute exists, plus verifying method name matching handles different cases like "POST", "Post", and missing attributes.

I should also consider testing relative action URLs resolved against a baseUri, which requires constructing form control elements (inputs, selects with options) by setting attributes like type and checked directly on Element instances.

Building test select elements with options...

I recall val() checks if the tag is textarea, returning text(), otherwise returning the value attribute -- so options with a "value" attr set will return that via val(). For checkboxes, val() similarly returns the value attribute if present, otherwise falls back to "on" when checked. I'm setting up a checkbox element with type, name, checked, and value attributes to confirm formData() picks up "yes" correctly.

Without a value attr, a checked checkbox defaults to "on"; radios work the same way with type="radio". Unchecked checkboxes get skipped entirely since there's no checked attribute. For a normal text input with name and value set, formData() should return the value directly, while disabled inputs or inputs missing a name attribute should be skipped -- assuming attr("name") returns an empty string when the attribute doesn't exist, which is standard jsoup behavior.

I also want to verify that non-form-submittable tags like a div are skipped, since Tag.valueOf("div").isFormSubmittable() should return false given that div isn't part of jsoup's defined form-listed/submittable tag set. I should double check this assumption to be safe.

Since I'm not fully certain of Tag's exact implementation here, I'll leave a comment flagging the assumption rather than asserting behavior not confirmed by the source. Now I'm shifting to testing submit() behavior, which requires inspecting the Connection object returned by Jsoup.connect(action).

I'm figuring out that calling form.submit() without execute() avoids any real network request, since Jsoup.connect just builds an HttpConnection instance. I can verify the request's URL and method through the Connection's request() accessor, checking that it matches the expected action URL and HTTP method.

For testing POST, I switch the form's method attribute to "post" and resubmit, expecting Connection.Method.POST on the resulting connection. I also plan to verify that Validate.notEmpty throws IllegalArgumentException when the form has no action attribute and an empty base URI, confirming submit() fails appropriately in that case.

When the form has a base URI but no action attribute, I expect submit() to fall back to the base URI itself as the request URL. For a relative action attribute combined with a base URI, I test that absUrl resolves them correctly into a full URL.

I should also test lowercase "post" to confirm the method attribute gets uppercased correctly, and verify no method attribute defaults to GET. I'm assuming Connection.KeyVal exposes key() and value() methods matching the real jsoup API, and that addElement() returns "this" for chaining, which I'll now write into the final test class.

I also want a combined test covering formData() with mixed element types—text input, checked checkbox, disabled field, select—to exercise the loop across branches together, alongside the isolated tests I already have. I'm double-checking the "select" tagName comparison is safe since Tag.valueOf normalizes to lowercase, so that match holds.

For checkbox/radio type matching I should verify the equalsIgnoreCase branch with mixed-case type attributes like "CheckBox" to confirm case-insensitive handling works, and I'll make sure I have the right imports lined up (Attributes, Tag, Element, Connection, FormElement) while skipping Jsoup import unless it's actually needed elsewhere.

The FormElement constructor needs a Tag, baseUri string, and an Attributes object. I'm thinking through edge cases like an empty baseUri with no action attribute, which should trigger a Validate.notEmpty exception since the resolved action would be blank -- a good test for the exception path when absUrl can't resolve a valid action.

I'll keep the test coverage focused: one path for hasAttr("action") being true with a resolvable absolute URL, another for it being false where the code falls back to baseUri, plus the exception cases already covered. That gives me tests like checking the action attribute resolves to an absolute URL with GET, verifying POST method handling in both uppercase and lowercase form, confirming the fallback to baseUri when no action attribute exists, and more.

For the implementation, I'm trusting that Connection.Request supports url() and method() as standard jsoup API methods, and that FormElement inherits attr(), hasAttr(), and val() from its parent Element/Node classes even though they're not shown in the snippet -- these are real jsoup behaviors I can rely on.
